# Suppress lock-order-inversion between RunningQueryPlan::start and QueryCatalog::start
# Currently, it is impossible that these two operations (targeting the same query) run concurrently.

deadlock:NES::RunningQueryPlan::start
deadlock:NES::QueryCatalog::start

# Suppress false positive race conditions in standard library's shared_ptr, weak_ptr, and future/promise implementations.
# These use lock-free atomic operations for reference counting which TSAN reports as races when the stdlib
# is not compiled with sanitizer instrumentation. These suppressions are specific to known safe patterns
# and do not hide races in our code's usage of these standard library components.
# TODO #808: These suppressions will be removed once we introduce a sanitized standard library.
race:std::__future_base
race:_Sp_counted_ptr_inplace
race:_Sp_counted_base
race:std::__libcpp_atomic_refcount_decrement
race:weak_ptr
race:__shared_count
race:__shared_weak_count
race:__assoc_state
race:__assoc_sub_state

# Codon constructs a fresh LLVM compiler for every Python UDF it compiles, and its LLVMVisitor
# constructor calls LLVMInitializeX86Target/TargetMC/AsmPrinter, which write LLVM's global target
# registry (llvm::getTheX86_64Target()'s Target object) with the values it already holds. Nautilus
# reads that same registry when it creates a target machine for a query pipeline, and both run on
# worker threads, so TSan reports a write/read race on the registry. Re-registration writes identical
# values, which is why it is harmless in practice. Removing the suppression needs Codon to register the
# targets once, before any worker thread exists, which its public API does not expose today.
race:codon::ir::LLVMVisitor::LLVMVisitor
# The registering frames themselves, in case the Codon constructor cannot be symbolized
# (the patterns match as substrings, so TargetMC is covered too).
race:LLVMInitializeX86Target
race:LLVMInitializeX86AsmPrinter
